premise: What if the Moon vanished? (a wizard sneezes it away; every consequence is real, sourced science)
title:
WHAT IF THE
MOON JUST
VANISHED?

lines.text: What if a wizard sneezed, and the Moon just vanished?
Poof. Three hundred eighty four thousand kilometres of empty sky.

facts.claim: NASA: the Moon is an average of 384,400 km away.
facts.quote: The Moon is an average of 238,855 miles (384,400 kilometers) away

lines.text: First, the oceans notice. The Moon's gravity makes the bulges that give us high tides.

facts.claim: NASA: the Moon's pull makes the oceans bulge on both sides; these bulges create high tides.
facts.quote: causes the oceans to bulge out on both the side closest to the Moon and the side farthest from the Moon

lines.text: The Sun still pulls, but its tide force is only about half the Moon's. So the tides shrink.

facts.claim: NOAA: the sun's tide-generating force is about half that of the moon.
facts.quote: the sun's tide-generating force is about half that of the moon

lines.text: Nights get darker. No moonlight. Just stars.
And total solar eclipses are gone forever. Only the Moon can block the whole face of the Sun.

facts.claim: NASA: a total solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, completely blocking the face of the Sun.
facts.quote: completely blocking the face of the Sun

lines.text: Fun part: we only ever saw one side of it. The same face, all the time.

facts.claim: NASA: synchronous rotation, so the same hemisphere faces Earth all the time.
facts.quote: so the same hemisphere faces Earth all the time

lines.text: So the wizard puts it back. But it's already drifting away, about an inch every year.

facts.claim: NASA: the Moon is getting about an inch farther away each year.
facts.quote: getting about an inch farther away each year

lines.text: So look up tonight. It's leaving us. Very, very slowly.
